jobs.occupation: Research Associate (m/f/d), EG 14 TV-H (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: Research Associate (m/f/d), EG 14 TV-H, fixed-term, full-time (currently 40 hours per week)Application deadline:20.11.2026Date of hire:01.01.2027vacancy number:39545The post is initially limited until 31 December 2028 as part of the ‘DyNaMo’ project, in accordance with its duration (academic qualification position pursuant to § 2 WissZeitVG).  An extension of the employment is planned. The opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree is given.The Intelligent Embedded Systems (IES) group conducts research in the area of fundamentals and applications of methods in data analysis, machine learning (e.g. deep learning, active learning) and artificial intelligence. In the focus of basic research are, for example, self-learning and self-organizing systems, methods of collaborative and active learning, methods of transfer learning, and techniques for real-time analysis of time series. Applied research focuses on the fields of energy systems, automotive (autonomous driving) and experimental physics/materials. The IES group currently employs around 20 researchers in the above areas.Your tasks:- Methods for perceiving cyclists’ behaviour by using machine learning techniques (in particular deep learning approaches) based on data from vehicle sensors (e.g. camera and LiDAR data).- Cross-labelling approaches for the highly automated annotation of cyclists’ behaviour data, i.e. transferring ‘labels’ from, for example, camera data to LiDAR data.- Methods for integrating information from models trained on different data modalities and evaluating the resulting information gain.- Planning and conducting measurement campaigns in the form of laboratory experiments as well as field experiments.- Research within the DyNaMo project.- Contributing to the group’s general tasks.Requirements:- A PhD and a completed university degree in Computer Science or a closely related field- Excellent knowledge in perception and computer vision.- Very good fundamental knowledge in machine learning and data analysis.- A successful academic career with high-impact publications in the relevant fields.- Experience in external fundraising (e.g. LOEWE, BMFTR, DFG).- Experience in programming, particularly in Python, but also in other programming languages.- Good knowledge of AI tools, e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Pandas, OpenCV and NumPy.- A structured approach to work that enables you to lead a team.- A keen interest in the challenges posed by machine learning applications in the field of automated driving.- An independent and goal-oriented approach to work, and a passion for scientific research.- Very good written and spoken German and English (at least B2 level in each).- A driving licence valid in Germany for passenger cars.The following conditions are advantageous- Experience in organisation and coordination (e.g. project management, team leadership).- Experience in supervising PhD students, e.g. when they write publications.As a member of staff in the Intelligent Embedded Systems group:- You will lead a small but highly motivated team,- you will have the opportunity to attend conferences, summer schools, and various professional development programmes (e.g. the opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree),- you will have access to your own, very large Slurm-based compute cluster (CPU and GPU),- you will have access to your own, state-of-the-art test vehicle (a car equipped with a camera, LiDAR and radar),- you will be able to develop new methods for use in practical applications.In case of any questions ask Prof. Dr. B. Sick, bsick(at)uni-kassel.deErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Programmiersprache Python, Datenanalyse, Machine LearningExpertenkenntnisse: Bilderkennung

jobs.occupation: PhD Position on Femtosecond Spectroscopy of Chiral Molecular Ions (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Job available in 2 locations: Kassel, BremenWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionA PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.About the TRILOGY Doctoral NetworkTRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.About the PhD ProjectThe selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.Key Research Activities- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.Candidate ProfileApplicants should have:- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection- Excellent written and spoken English.- Good written and oral communication skills.- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.MSCA Mobility and Eligibility RequirementsAs the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.Application DocumentsApplications should include:- Cover letter- Detailed curriculum vitae- Academic transcripts- Copy of the Master's thesis- Scientific publication, if available- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.Selection ProcessCandidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.Key InformationPosition: PhD Researcher / Doctoral CandidateNumber of positions: 1Research areas: Physics, Engineering, ChemistryResearcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)Contract: Temporary, full-timeWorking hours: 35 hours per weekCountry: GermanyWork locations: Bremen and KasselFunding: Horizon Europe – Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral NetworkProject: TRILOGYMarie Curie Grant Agreement: 101226887If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter.At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. jobs.occupation: PhD Student (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Your applicationPlease submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable.We look forward to receiving your application!Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.Your tasks•  Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil.•  Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses.•  Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility.•  Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico.•  Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings.Your qualifications•  Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field.•  Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided.•  Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning.•  Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research.•  Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English.•  Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite.We offer•  A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration.•  Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise.•  An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences.•  Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies.•  Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified.This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration.The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT.
